column1: The concept of the rocket, or rather the mechanism behind the idea of propelling an object into the air, has been around for well over two thousand years.
column2: 火箭的概念，或者说推动物体升空的原理，已有两千多年历史。

column1: However, it wasn’t until the discovery of the reaction principle, which was the key to space travel and so represents one of the great milestones in the history of scientific thought, that rocket technology was able to develop.
column2: 然而，直到反应原理被发现之后，火箭技术才得以发展。这一原理正是实现太空旅行的关键，因此可以说它是科学思想史上的一座重要里程碑。

column1: Not only did it solve a problem that had intrigued man for ages, but, more importantly, it literally opened the door to the exploration of the universe.
column2: 它不仅解决了一个困扰人类多年的问题，更重要的是，它真正打开了探索宇宙的大门。

column1: An intellectual breakthrough, brilliant though it may be, does not automatically ensure that the transition is made from theory to practice.
column2: 一个智力上的突破，即使非常出色，也不能自动保证从理论转向实践。

column1: Despite the fact that rockets had been used sporadically for several hundred years, they remained a relatively minor artefact of civilization until the twentieth century.
column2: 尽管火箭在几个世纪里一直被偶尔使用，但直到20世纪为止，它们仍然只是文明中较为次要的产物而已。

column1: Prodigious efforts, accelerated during two world wars, were required before the technology of primitive rocketry could be translated into the reality of sophisticated astronauts.
column2: 在两次世界大战期间，人们付出了巨大的努力，才使得原始的火箭技术能够转化为实际可行的、适用于宇航员飞行的技术。

column1: It is strange that the rocket was generally ignored by writers of fiction to transport their heroes to mysterious realms beyond the Earth, even though it had been commonly used in fireworks displays in China since the thirteenth century.
column2: 奇怪的是，尽管早在十三世纪中国就已广泛用于烟火表演，小说家们却普遍忽视了火箭作为交通工具将英雄送入地球之外神秘领域的可能性。

column1: The reason is that nobody associated the reaction principle with the idea of traveling through space to a neighbouring world.
column2: 原因是没有人将反应原理与‘穿越太空到邻近世界’的设想联系起来。

column1: A simple analogy can help us to understand how a rocket operates.
column2: 一个简单的类比可以帮助我们理解火箭的工作原理。

column1: It is much like a machine gun mounted on the rear of a boat.
column2: 它就像一门安装在船尾的机枪。

column1: In reaction to the backward discharge of bullets, the gun, and hence the boat, move forwards.
column2: 由于子弹向后喷出，枪和船会向前移动。

column1: A rocket motor’s ‘bullets’ are minute, high-speed particles produced by burning propellants in a suitable chamber.
column2: 火箭发动机的‘子弹’是指在适当燃烧室中燃烧推进剂所产生的微小、高速粒子。

column1: The reaction to the ejection of these small particles causes the rocket to move forwards.
column2: 这些微小颗粒的喷出产生反作用力，使火箭向前移动。

column1: There is evidence that the reaction principle was applied practically well before the rocket was invented.
column2: 有证据表明，这种反应原理在火箭发明之前就已经被实际应用。

column1: In his Noctes Atticae or Greek Nights, Aulus Gellius describes ‘the pigeon of Archytas’, an invention dating back to about 360 BC.
column2: 奥卢斯·格利乌斯在《阿提卡之夜》（文中亦称《希腊之夜》）中描述了“阿尔基塔斯的鸽子”。这项发明可追溯到约公元前360年。
column4: Greek Nights|n. 原文所用的另一书名

column1: Cylindrical in shape, made of wood, and hanging from string, it was moved to and fro by steam blowing out from small exhaust ports at either end.
column2: 呈圆柱形、由木头制成、悬挂在绳子上的装置，通过两端小排气口喷出的蒸汽推动来回运动。

column1: The reaction to the discharging steam provided the bird with motive power.
column2: 蒸汽排出产生的反作用力为鸟提供了动力。

column1: The invention of rockets is linked inextricably with the invention of ‘black powder’.
column2: 火箭的发明与‘黑火药’的发明密不可分。

column1: Most historians of technology credit the Chinese with its discovery.
column2: 大多数技术史学家认为，火箭的发明属于中国人。

column1: They base their belief on studies of Chinese writings or on the notebooks of early Europeans who settled in or made long visits to China to study its history and civilisation.
column2: 他们的信念基于对中国文献的研究，以及早期定居在中国或多次访问中国的欧洲人的笔记记录。这些记录帮助他们了解中国的历史与文明。

column1: It was not until the eighteenth century that Europe became seriously interested in the possibilities of using the rocket itself as a weapon of war and not just to propel other weapons.
column2: 直到18世纪，欧洲才开始真正关注将火箭本身作为战争武器使用的可能性，而不仅仅是用来推动其他武器。

column1: Prior to this, rockets were used only in pyrotechnic displays.
column2: 在此之前，火箭仅被用于烟火表演。

column1: The incentive for the more aggressive use of rockets came not from within the European continent but from far-away India, whose leaders had built up a corps of rocketeers and used rockets successfully against the British in the late eighteenth century.
column2: 推动人们更积极使用火箭的动力并非来自欧洲大陆内部，而是来自遥远的印度。在18世纪末期，印度的领导人组建了一支火箭部队，并成功运用火箭武器对抗英国军队。

column1: In the early nineteenth century, the British began to experiment with incendiary barrage rockets.
column2: 在19世纪初，英国人开始尝试使用燃烧弹进行轰炸。

column1: The Americans developed a rocket, complete with its own launcher, to use against the Mexicans in the mid-nineteenth century.
column2: 在19世纪中期，美国人研制出一种配备专用发射台的火箭，用于攻击墨西哥人。

column1: However, the results were sometimes not that impressive as the behaviour of the rockets in flight was less than predictable.
column2: 然而，结果有时并不令人满意，因为火箭在飞行过程中的行为难以预测。

column1: Since then, there have been huge developments in rocket technology, often with devastating results in the forum of war.
column2: 从那时起，火箭技术取得了巨大发展，但在战争领域往往带来了毁灭性的后果。

column1: Nevertheless, the modern day space programs owe their success to the humble beginnings of those in previous centuries who developed the foundations of the reaction principle.
column2: 尽管如此，现代航天计划的成功归功于几个世纪前那些为反作用原理奠定基础的先驱们。

column1: Who knows what it will be like in the future?
column2: 谁知道未来会是什么样子呢？
